## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Pattanillehaka* ("Licking the almsbowl") is the fifty-third training rule (*sekhiya*) in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates monastic deportment while eating from the almsbowl. An English translation of the rule and its Vinaya analysis has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Corresponding rules exist in the Pali Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, and Parivāra, as well as in the monastic codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages extant in Sanskrit, Chinese translation, and Tibetan translation.

Pali-internal text reuse calculated by DharmaNexus detects 84 matching passages across 38 texts, reflecting the standardized framing and vocabulary of the *sekhiya* section [DharmaNexus]. Its highest internal reuse occurs with adjacent dining etiquette rules, notably Sekhiya 52 and Sekhiya 54 (both matching §0.1–1.7 at over 0.90 similarity), alongside Sekhiya 35, 44, 45, and 47 [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns segments of the rule with Jayarakṣita's Sanskrit commentary, the *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
